pl-l2d21c1-d1e108.summary: Seeing that man could ascend by obedient humility to where he had fallen by pride, the devil envied him; once diabolus ('falling down') by pride, he became Satan ('adversary') by envy. He tempted the woman, in whom reason was weaker, attacking human nature at its weaker part so that, if he prevailed, he might approach the stronger with more confidence.
claims: He attacked the woman as the weaker part.

pl-l2d21c1.summary: Begins the account of the fall. Seeing that man could rise by humble obedience where he had fallen by pride, the devil envied him and from diabolus became Satan, adversary. He tempted the woman, in whom reason was weaker, attacking human nature at its weaker point, so that if he prevailed he could approach the stronger part with more confidence.
claims: The devil envied man's ability to rise by obedience where he had fallen by pride.
Envy made the devil Satan, the adversary.
He tempted the woman first, attacking the weaker point.
